providers.title: The energy of a lattice
providers.scope: A lattice of covolume one in the plane has density one, and its energy for any nonnegative interaction is the sum of the interaction over the nonzero lattice vectors, finite or not.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The linear programming bound for configurations of density one
providers.scope: If a continuous even function with suitable decay has a nonnegative Fourier transform, then for every locally finite planar configuration of centred density one the lower limit of the averaged sums of the function over pairs is at least the transform at zero minus the function at zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The bound and lattices
providers.scope: The linear programming bound is at most the energy of every lattice of covolume one, with equality exactly when the function touches the interaction at the nonzero lattice points and its transform vanishes at the nonzero dual lattice points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gaussian optimality from a sharp pair
providers.scope: If a sharp pair exists for a Gaussian interaction, every configuration of density one has at least the energy of the triangular lattice for it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The moment problem on the unit interval
providers.scope: A sequence all of whose iterated differences alternate in sign is the sequence of moments of exactly one finite positive Borel measure on the unit interval.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Completely monotone functions as mixtures
providers.scope: A completely monotone function on the closed half-line is the integral of the functions v^t against a finite positive measure on the unit interval, of total mass the value at zero and without mass at zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From Gaussians to completely monotone interactions
providers.scope: A planar configuration of density one that has at least the energy of the triangular lattice for every Gaussian interaction has at least its energy for every completely monotone interaction of the squared distance, in the extended nonnegative reals.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Universal optimality from sharp Gaussian pairs
providers.scope: If a sharp pair exists for every Gaussian, the triangular lattice has the least energy among planar configurations of density one for every completely monotone interaction of the squared distance.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Residues of the triangular form
providers.scope: Every integer of the form j^2 + j l + l^2 is congruent to 0, 1, 3, 4, 7 or 9 modulo 12.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The dual of the triangular lattice
providers.scope: The dual lattice of the triangular lattice of covolume one is the lattice turned by a right angle.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Fourier transform of a planar Gaussian
providers.scope: The Fourier transform of exp(-pi beta |x|^2) on the plane is exp(-pi |xi|^2 / beta) divided by beta.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gaussian duality
providers.scope: If the normalized statement holds for every parameter k at least 2.36, there is a radial sharp pair for every Gaussian.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Fourier coefficients of the sine product
providers.scope: The product of the squares of 2 sin(pi (s - a)/12) over a = 0, 1, 3, 4, 7, 9 is a trigonometric polynomial with frequencies l/6, l from -6 to 6, and coefficients 5, -1 + i sqrt 3, 1 + i sqrt 3, -2, (-1 + i sqrt 3)/2, -1 - i sqrt 3, 1 for l = 0 to 6 and their conjugates for negative l.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The sine product at its zeros
providers.scope: At each of its real zeros the sine product has a double zero with leading coefficient above 7/4 and relative next coefficient below 53/25 in absolute value; both are given in closed form for the six residue classes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cardinal functions
providers.scope: For a summable coefficient list the cardinal function is entire, real on the real axis, has value and derivative at each node determined by the two coefficients of that node, and is the sum of a multiple of the sine product and the integral of exponentials with frequencies between -1 and 1 against a density of integral at most 36 times the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Uniform bounds for cardinal functions
providers.scope: The j-th derivative of a cardinal function is bounded on the real axis by pi^j (25 |C| + 36 W), with W the sum of the absolute values of the pole coefficients, wherever the nonzero coefficients sit.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Fourier transform of a planar Gaussian with a complex parameter
providers.scope: For a complex number gamma with positive real part, the Fourier transform of exp(-pi gamma |x|^2) on the plane is exp(-pi |xi|^2 / gamma) divided by gamma.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fourier pairs from cardinal functions
providers.scope: For a cardinal function p there is an entire function K, real on the real axis and decaying exponentially on the half-line with all derivatives, such that exp(-pi h s) p(s) and exp(-pi h s) K(s), with s = (sqrt 3 / 2)|x|^2 and h = 2/5, are Fourier transforms of each other on the plane.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The coupled pair
providers.scope: For two coefficient lists the functions H_1 = p_1 + K_{p_2} and H_2 = p_2 + K_{p_1} give an admissible radial function exp(-pi h s) H_1(s) with Fourier transform exp(-pi h s) H_2(s); if they satisfy the contact and sign conditions, the normalized statement holds.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The norm of the jet operator
providers.scope: The operator S that sends a coefficient list to minus the jet list of its transformed function maps into summable lists, with the sum of absolute values at most 4000 times that of the input list.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The transformed kernel on two frequency ranges
providers.scope: For frequencies of absolute value at most 5/6 the kernel decays at the rate 0.70; between 5/6 and 1 it is smaller in size and decays at the rate 0.187 + 2.48 (1 - |t|).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Refined bounds for the transformed function
providers.scope: The transformed function of a cardinal function and its derivatives are bounded on the positive half-line by a term with the rate 0.70 plus a term with the rate 0.187 whose part coming from the pole coefficients carries a factor 1/s.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tail bound for the jet operator
providers.scope: The sum of the absolute values of the output of the jet operator at the nodes n >= r is at most U_r(w, c) = 800 (w + c) e^(-0.70 r)/(1 - e^(-0.70)) + 5.3 (2.54 w/r + 2c) e^(-0.187 r)/(1 - e^(-0.187)), where w bounds the pole coefficients and c the constant entry of the list.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first rule of Fejér
providers.scope: For even N the rule with the points cos(pi (v + 1/2)/N) and the weights o_v gives the average over [-1, 1] of every polynomial of degree at most N - 1; the weights are at least 1/(N(N - 1)) and add up to 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The error of the rule for holomorphic functions
providers.scope: For a function holomorphic and bounded by A on the closed disc of twice the radius of the interval, the average over the interval and the rule differ by at most 4A 2^(-N).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quadrature error for the spectral integrals
providers.scope: With 384 points on each of the six frequency intervals, the values and scaled derivatives y^a p^(a)(s)/a! and y^a K^(a)(s)/a! for a list with one unit entry at a node up to 168, for 0 <= s <= 168 and |y| <= 3/2, differ from their quadrature forms by less than 10^-31.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The jet matrix and its quadrature form
providers.scope: On lists that vanish beyond the node 168, every entry of the matrix of the jet operator at the nodes up to 168 differs from its quadrature form by less than 2 x 10^-31.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The residual of the reference columns
providers.scope: The reference columns satisfy X_1 - D X_2 = g_1 - D^512 g_1 and X_2 - D X_1 = g_2 - D^512 g_2 on the nodes up to 168.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Norm bounds for the finite matrices (computed)
providers.scope: The matrix D^64 has column-sum norm below 0.004, the two finite geometric sums have norms adding up to less than 36, and the columns of the two reference matrices have total l^1 norm below 2.3 (columns 1 to 5) and 5.6 (columns 6 to 10). Established by a computation in ball arithmetic; the program is printed in the lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The size of the reference lists
providers.scope: For every parameter k at least 2.36 the two reference lists have total l^1 norm below 4.8 and constant entries of total absolute value below 0.02, and D^512 has norm below 0.004^8.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The inverse of the finite block
providers.scope: The block of the interpolation operator on the nodes up to 168 is invertible, with inverse of norm less than 40.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The interpolation operator is invertible
providers.scope: The operator (a_1, a_2) -> (a_1 - S a_2, a_2 - S a_1) is a bijection of the space of pairs of summable lists on the nodes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact interpolation
providers.scope: For every k at least 2.36 the interpolation system has exactly one solution with the chosen extra entries; it differs from the reference lists by less than 2 x 10^-8 in total l^1 norm, and the two lists have total norm less than 5.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The functions with contacts at all nodes
providers.scope: For every k at least 2.36 there are entire functions H_1, H_2, real on the real axis, with H_1 = T_k, H_1' = T_k', H_2 = 0, H_2' = 0 at every node, such that exp(-pi h s) H_1(s) is an admissible radial function with Fourier transform exp(-pi h s) H_2(s); the normalized statement follows if H_1 <= T_k and H_2 >= 0 on the half-line.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The quotient for the exact and the reference lists
providers.scope: On every half-gap the quotients of the functions of the exact lists and of the reference lists, after the value and the slope at the centre are removed, differ by less than 0.00011.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The polynomial of degree 40
providers.scope: On every half-gap the quotient of the reference function differs by less than 10^-6 from the polynomial of degree 40 whose coefficients are the quadrature forms of its scaled derivatives at the centre.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Lower supports of the target
providers.scope: For k between two consecutive endpoints K < J of the list 2.36, 2.65, 3.2, 4, 6, infinity, the quotient of T_k on a half-gap is at least an explicit polynomial depending only on K, J and the half-gap, minus 10^-6.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Reduction of the sign conditions on the bounded range
providers.scope: If the polynomials Phi_i(x; k) are at least 0.001 on [0, 1] for all 91 half-gaps and both indices, then T_k - H_1 and H_2 are nonnegative on [0, 89.5].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Containing parameter boxes
providers.scope: For k between two consecutive endpoints K < J, a linear expression in the ten numbers q(k) is at least the bracket [l]_{K,J}, the smaller of two values of a concave lower envelope formed from the corners of a box that contains the curve q(k).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bernstein coefficients
providers.scope: A polynomial of degree at most 40 is on [0, 1] at least the smallest of its Bernstein coefficients of degree 40, which are the sums of binomial(d, r)/binomial(40, r) times its coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The inequalities on the half-gaps (computed)
providers.scope: For the 91 half-gaps, both indices, the five parameter intervals and the 41 Bernstein indices, the lower bounds for the Bernstein coefficients of the polynomials Phi_i are larger than 0.001. Established by a computation in ball arithmetic; the program is printed in the lesson.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The sign conditions on the bounded range
providers.scope: For every k at least 2.36 the functions of the exact interpolation satisfy H_1 <= T_k and H_2 >= 0 on [0, 89.5].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A quadratic lower bound for the sine product
providers.scope: For every real s and a zero m of the sine product nearest to s, P(s) is at least 0.68 (s - m)^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The sign conditions beyond 89.5
providers.scope: For every k at least 2.36 the functions of the exact interpolation satisfy H_1 <= T_k and H_2 >= 0 on the half-line from 89.5.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The normalized statement
providers.scope: For every real k at least 2.36 there are entire functions H_1, H_2, real on the real axis, such that exp(-pi h s) H_1(s) is an admissible radial function with Fourier transform exp(-pi h s) H_2(s), with H_1 <= T_k and H_2 >= 0 on the half-line and with equal values and first derivatives of H_1 and T_k, and of H_2 and 0, at every node.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Universal optimality of the triangular lattice
providers.scope: For every completely monotone interaction of the squared distance, every configuration of density one in the plane has at least the energy of the triangular lattice of covolume one. Three steps of the proof are finite computations with rigorous error bounds, with the programs printed in the lessons.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gaussian energies of periodic configurations
providers.scope: For a periodic configuration C of density one, H_C(t) = (1/N) sum of P_t(a_i - a_j) - Psi_t(0) equals the energy of C for the Gaussian exp(-u/(4t)) divided by 4 pi t; it depends only on the set C, and H_C(t) >= H_A(t) for the triangular lattice A and every t > 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fourier coefficients of the periodic kernel
providers.scope: The periodic kernel K_{s,L}, defined as a heat integral with sigma = 1 - s/2, is integrable over a cell and has the Fourier coefficients (4 pi^2 |xi|^2)^(-sigma) at the nonzero points of the dual lattice and 0 at 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The singular part of the periodic kernel
providers.scope: K_{s,L}(x) - g_s(x)/q_s has a limit at 0, where g_s = |x|^-s (0 < s < 2) or -log|x| (s = 0) and q_s = 2^(2-s) pi Gamma(1-s/2)/Gamma(s/2) (q_0 = 2 pi); the limit is given by a heat integral over the nonzero lattice points.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The periodic energy as an integral of Gaussian energies
providers.scope: For 0 < s < 2 the periodic energy of a periodic configuration C of density one is q_s/Gamma(1-s/2) times the integral over t of (H_C(t) - 1) t^(-s/2); for s = 0 the same with a correction 1/(4 pi t) for t > 1 and a constant. It depends only on the set C.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Comparison across period lattices
providers.scope: For periodic configurations C, D of density one with any period lattices and 0 <= s < 2: V_s(C) - V_s(D) = q_s/Gamma(1-s/2) times the absolutely convergent integral of (H_C(t) - H_D(t)) t^(-s/2).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The triangular lattice minimizes the periodic Riesz and logarithmic energies
providers.scope: For 0 <= s < 2, every periodic configuration of density one in the plane has at least the periodic energy of order s of the triangular lattice of covolume one. The proof uses the theorem of the course for all Gaussians.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
